description: Adds an iterated local search (SLSQP restarted from perturbed copies of the best packing) with the centre perturbation sd adapted online: x1.2 on improvement, x0.95 on failure, clipped to [0.005, 0.1], starting at 0.03. The current script has no ILS, so the perturbation loop is introduced here rather than edited.
Adds a two-stage SLSQP per restart: first maximise sum(r**0.97) from random starts, then polish with the true linear sum of radii from that solution before repair.

For a random half of the starts, run a symmetric SLSQP stage over the free variables of a diagonal-reflection-symmetric parametrisation (linear map M), then run the unchanged full unconstrained SLSQP from that symmetric solution.

Replaces the greedy shrink in _repair with an exact HiGHS LP that maximises the sum of radii for fixed centres, keeping the old shrink loop as a safety net for LP tolerance, since the 1e-12 margin alone would not pass the 1e-10 check.
Initialise centres uniformly on [0.05, 0.95] and radii uniformly on [0.02, 0.15] instead of a constant 0.05, so SLSQP starts from varied size distributions and reaches more diverse basins.

Adds a hexagonal-lattice start (random rotation, spacing, offset, the 26 points nearest a random interior spot, jittered, radii = nearest-neighbour distance / 2.5) used for a random half of the restarts alongside the uniform random starts.

Adds a large-neighbourhood destroy-and-repair step: after the first random restart, each iteration re-randomises the circles inside a random disc of radius 0.25 to 0.35 in the incumbent packing, reruns SLSQP from that start, and keeps the result only if its radius sum improves.

issues: No integrity problems: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, seeded RNG used, packing still repaired and checked by the harness.

Design flaw, not a validity bug: the L-BFGS-B penalty result pv.x is used only to screen starts; SLSQP restarts from the original x0, so the penalty work is thrown away and fewer starts get the full solve. This probably explains the regression.
Each loop now does extra L-BFGS work before SLSQP, but the time check is unchanged (top of loop, TIME_FRACTION 0.8), so the risk of running over is about the same as the incumbent's.
Recomputed z = (-2.6280 - -2.6219) / (0.0023*sqrt(1+1/10)) ≈ -2.53, which matches the harness's -2.535 up to rounding. The candidate is worse; rejection is justified (1 run only).

description: Adds a cheap penalty-based screen: each random start first gets 60 L-BFGS-B iterations on a bounded overlap-penalty objective, and full SLSQP runs only if its repaired radius sum is in the top third of starts seen so far.
Adds a radius-cap continuation to each SLSQP restart: caps rise from 0.05 to 0.4 in steps of 0.02 with warm starts, then a final solve at cap 1.0 (effectively uncapped).
Pass exact analytic Jacobians for the SLSQP objective and all constraints so each restart avoids finite-difference evaluations and runs faster.

Adds an elite pool of the top 8 distinct packings, and after the first two packings each SLSQP start is seeded by crossing left-of-split centres from one random parent with right-of-split centres from another, filling any gap with random centres.

Before the radius-cap SLSQP continuation, each restart first minimises a smooth penalty (minus sum of radii plus geometrically rising weight times squared pair and boundary violations, weights 10 to 1e6 over 5 stages) with L-BFGS-B, and uses the result as the SLSQP warm start.

Adds an equal-radius SLSQP stage (maximise a common radius t over the centres and t, 2n+1 variables) at the start of each restart, and uses its centres with radii set to t as the start for the free-radius continuation.

On every other start, remove the smallest-radius circle of the best packing, reinsert it at the most open of 2000 random sample points, reset all radii to INIT_RADIUS, and rerun SLSQP from that configuration; the existing keep-if-better logic is unchanged.

Each restart solves a packing for n+1 circles with the radius-cap SLSQP continuation, drops the smallest-radius circle, and runs one short SLSQP polish with n circles before the unchanged repair and best-of-restarts selection.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. All randomness comes from the seeded rng passed into _mc_start.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. MC moves are accepted only if they keep the current radii valid. _grow sets radii conservatively (r_i <= min(wall, d_ij/2)), and the existing SLSQP and repair steps still run on the result. The result can therefore be checked by the harness exactly as before.

Minor wording problem: the docstring calls this 'compression', but it is a random shake at fixed radii followed by regrowing the radii once per sweep. Also, _grow returns a valid lower bound, not the 'largest radii'. This does not affect correctness.

Minor cost: each restart spends about 100*26 Python-level steps on MC, so fewer SLSQP restarts fit in the 80% time budget. The start still respects the time limit because it runs inside the existing loop.

z could not be reproduced exactly. With a difference of 0.0001 and sd 0.0023, z is about 0.031 if both single runs are counted (se = 0.0023*sqrt(2)) and about 0.043 if only one sd is used. The reported 0.051 fits the rounding of the shown means (difference between 0.00005 and 0.00015). Either way z is far below any acceptance threshold, so 'reject' is consistent with the numbers.
Each side has only one run. A gain of 0.0001 is well inside the noise (sd 0.0023), so these numbers show no evidence of improvement.

description: Replaces the random uniform start in each SLSQP restart with a hard-disk Monte Carlo compression (100 sweeps of accepted random displacements, with radii regrown after each sweep), keeping the radius-cap continuation and repair unchanged.

Starts each SLSQP restart with radii drawn from a shuffled power-law profile (k^-0.5, total area about 0.6) instead of a uniform small radius, leaving the cap continuation, repair and selection unchanged.

Replaces the random restarts with a diagonal-step evolution strategy over the centres (12 candidates per generation, fast radii plus repair for ranking, mean from the best quarter, step scaled by success rate), and runs the radius-cap SLSQP polish only on each generation's best candidate.
Basin hopping from the incumbent: perturb the best packing with Gaussian noise and reset radii to 0.9x, then accept the new local optimum only if it improves the sum of radii.

Builds the SLSQP pair constraints only for centre pairs closer than 2*max(radius)+0.1, recomputed before each radius-cap pass, so each solve has fewer constraints; _repair still checks all pairs, so validity is unchanged.

Replaces the uniform random SLSQP start with a greedy max-min sequential initialisation (500-sample farthest-point placement against centres and walls), with radii set to half the minimum nearest-neighbour distance.
Multiplies each initial SLSQP radius by an independent uniform [0.5, 1.5] factor (clipped at zero) on every random start, so radii vary per start instead of all starting at INIT_RADIUS.

Builds the 26-circle packing by first finding the best 25-circle packing in the first third of the time, then inserting one circle at the largest-clearance point of a random sample, and running the capped SLSQP continuation on all 26 with the best packing kept.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and randomness comes only from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. Packings from the new permutation move still go through clip and _repair, so the harness check still applies. Starting SLSQP from a permuted, infeasible point with only caps=[1.0] is allowed, and the repair step makes the result valid.

Recomputed z: (-2.6318 - (-2.6343)) / (0.0023*sqrt(2)) = 0.0025/0.00325 = 0.77 in magnitude, with the candidate worse. The harness reports -0.746. The gap comes from rounding the shown values to 4 decimals: a difference of about 0.00243 gives 0.746. The two agree.

Evidence is weak: one run each. The candidate is about 0.0025 worse, roughly 1 noise sd, so rejecting is reasonable but not conclusive. The diff makes no performance claims, so nothing contradicts the numbers.

description: Adds radius-permutation moves: on each iteration after the first, with probability 0.5, shuffle the radii of a random pair or triple of circles on the best packing, re-optimise with SLSQP from those centres (cap 1.0), repair, and keep the result only if it beats the best.

Adds a growing centre box to the radius-cap SLSQP continuation: centre bounds start at [0.1, 0.9] in the first stage and expand linearly to [0, 1] at the last stage, passed via SLSQP's bounds argument, with the cap schedule and _repair unchanged.

Replaces the SLSQP local solver with a trust-region sequential LP (HiGHS linprog on linearised pair, wall and cap constraints, 60 iterations per cap stage) while keeping the radius-cap continuation and _repair.

Replaces the per-restart SLSQP solver with an augmented Lagrangian (PHR) method using L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients, keeping the radius-cap continuation, with 4 outer rounds per cap and rho growing by 3x each round.

Adds a deflation penalty to each restart's cap-continuation SLSQP objective that repels centres from the centres of up to 20 earlier converged packings (Gaussian kernel, s=0.15, weight 0.02 decaying linearly to 0 at the final cap=1.0 stage so the returned packing is an unpenalised local optimum).

Adds a Coulomb repulsion penalty 0.01*sum(1/(d^2+1e-4)) with analytic centre gradient to every radius-cap SLSQP stage below cap 0.4, halving it every 0.02 of cap so it is effectively gone before the final cap=1.0 stage.

On a random half of the SLSQP restarts, the centres start on a perimeter ring (about 4*sqrt(n) circles with a random offset along the four sides) plus the remaining circles uniformly in the inner square, with small radii; the other half keep the uniform start.
Replaces the uniform random centre start in each SLSQP restart with a seeded, digit-scrambled Halton point set (bases 2 and 3) on [0.1, 0.9]^2 plus uniform jitter of 0.02.
Abort: caching the pair indices and preallocating buffers would save almost no CPU time, because SLSQP's internal dense linear algebra dominates each restart.

Replaces the uniform random start in each restart with a Delaunay hole-filling build (3 random seeds, then repeatedly add the circumcentre of the largest hole among the top 3 chosen by rng, radius = distance to nearest centre or wall), which then feeds the existing radius-cap SLSQP continuation.

After each restart's radius-cap continuation, re-seed rattlers (circles with fewer than 2 contacts within 1e-6) at random points with radius 0.01, run one extra SLSQP stage, and keep it only if the radius sum improves.
Skip restarts whose end-of-restart packing signature (sorted radii rounded to 2 decimals plus wall-touch count) matches an earlier one, to free CPU time for new basins.

Raise TIME_FRACTION to 0.92 and skip any restart whose start would push elapsed CPU time plus the longest restart seen so far past 0.95 of time_limit, so more restarts fit in the budget while staying well below the 45 s hard stop.

Adds simulated-annealing acceptance to a perturbation-based iterated local search: each new SLSQP optimum is kept if it beats the current packing or passes exp((new - current)/T) with T starting at 0.02 and decaying by 0.97 per iteration, while the best packing seen is tracked separately.

On a random third of the SLSQP restarts, pin four free circles to the corners with centres at (r, r), (1-r, r), (r, 1-r), (1-r, 1-r) and initial radius r drawn uniformly from [0.05, 0.2], keeping the other 22 starts and the rest of the restart procedure unchanged.
Aborted: rattler-core reduction and reinsertion is near-duplicate of slot 31 (re-seeding rattlers after the cap continuation), which was neutral at -2.6343, so no new edit is proposed.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. The new code uses no randomness, so seeding is unaffected. The existing repair step still enforces validity, so the result is meaningful.

Recomputed z: the difference in loss is -2.6313 - (-2.6343) = +0.0030, which is worse. The standard error is sqrt(0.0023^2/1 + 0.0023^2/1) = 0.00325, so the improvement z is -0.0030/0.00325 = -0.92. This matches the harness value of -0.922, and reject is consistent.

Misleading docstring: _lloyd is called with constant weights w = INIT_RADIUS^2, so the power diagram is just an ordinary Voronoi diagram. The weighting does nothing, which makes this plain Lloyd relaxation.

Cost: each restart now runs 20 iterations over 40,000 grid points x 26 centres with full distance arrays. That likely takes a noticeable share of each restart and cuts the number of SLSQP restarts within the 80% time budget. This is a plausible cause of the regression. It is not a validity bug, and the call stays well under 45 s.
Lloyd relaxation also removes much of the diversity between random restarts, because the starts converge toward similar centroidal layouts. That could hurt the multi-start search.
Evidence is thin: 1 run on each side, and |z| < 1, so the result is not significant either way. Rejecting is still reasonable given the extra code and no sign of a gain.

description: Relaxes the random initial centres with 20 power-diagram Lloyd iterations (200x200 grid, cell weight INIT_RADIUS squared) before the existing SLSQP radius-cap continuation.

Runs successive halving over batches of 40 random starts: each start gets 30 SLSQP iterations, the best 5 are re-run with the full MAX_ITER, and the best finished packing is kept, with batches repeated until the time budget is spent.

For a random half of the SLSQP restarts, build the start as 4 to 6 horizontal rows of 3 to 7 circles each (summing to 26), with per-row offsets and 0.02 coordinate noise, randomly transposed, before the usual radius-cap continuation.

Draws each SLSQP restart's cap-continuation schedule from a seeded prior (start cap in [0.03, 0.12], final intermediate cap in [0.25, 0.5], 8/12/16/20 steps via np.linspace, then cap 1.0) instead of the fixed 0.05 to 0.4 list.

On a random half of the restarts after the first, the best packing's centres get a random 2x2 affine strain (identity plus N(0, 0.03) entries), are re-centred on (0.5, 0.5) and clipped to [0.02, 0.98], and the radii are set to 0.8 times the incumbent before running the radius-cap SLSQP continuation with its first cap at the incumbent's largest radius.
Freeze-and-thaw of the rigid core: keep the contact-rigid core fixed and re-randomise only the loose circles for the next restart, then run the full radius-cap continuation.

Before each radius-cap SLSQP stage after the first, jitter the centres with Gaussian noise of sd 0.02*cap/0.4 (as the spec's formula states, so the noise grows with the cap, contrary to the spec's "shrinks" prose), clip to [0,1], and start that stage from the jittered point.

Before each SLSQP restart, a random half of the restarts start their centres from a 300-step tabu search over a 40x40 grid of candidate centres (min-gap score, 30-move tabu list) instead of uniform random points, keeping the incumbent cap-continuation schedule.

issues: No integrity problems found. The diff does not read files, paste coordinates or touch the harness. All randomness comes from rng, which is seeded.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The packing first grows in a w0 x h0 rectangle of area 1, with an aspect ratio between 0.8 and 1.25. The last loop then morphs that rectangle linearly into the unit square, ending at t=1 with W=H=1 and cap=1.0. So the final SLSQP solve has the same constraints as before, and the existing repair step still guarantees a valid packing.

Minor: the starting points are scaled by w0 and h0, so they start inside [INIT_LOW*w0, (1-INIT_LOW)*w0] and the matching range for h0. That is harmless. The method now runs 5 final SLSQP solves instead of 1, so it costs more per restart and fits fewer restarts in the time budget. This is a trade-off, not a bug.

Recomputed z: the gap is 2.6349 - 2.6343 = 0.0006. The standard error of the gap is 0.0023*sqrt(1/1+1/1) = 0.00325, so z = 0.18. That matches the reported 0.187 up to rounding of the displayed values. The gain is well within noise, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers. With only one run on each side the test has very little power.

description: Gives each SLSQP restart a random rectangle of aspect ratio log-uniform in [0.8, 1.25] with area 1, runs the radius-cap continuation inside that box, then morphs the box to the unit square over five SLSQP solves.
Replace the uniform random SLSQP start with a short damped particle simulation (overlap springs, wall springs, damping, thermostat kick, radius growth) before the radius-cap SLSQP continuation.
Batched projected-gradient population of 64 penalty-based starts before SLSQP, keeping the top 3 for the cap continuation.

Aborted without a job: a Poisson-disk start on half the restarts is another evenly spread start-shape change, the family the notes say to avoid (slots 5, 19, 20, 28, 29, 30, 34, 35, 37 and 41 were neutral or worse).

On a random half of the SLSQP restarts, replace the uniform random centre start with a sequential greedy build: circles are placed in seeded random order at the best of 2000 random candidates, with radius 0.9 times the largest feasible value, before the unchanged radius-cap SLSQP continuation.

Tolerance annealing across the radius-cap SLSQP continuation: loose ftol 1e-3 with 40 iterations for caps up to 0.2, ftol 1e-6 with 120 iterations for middle caps, and ftol 1e-12 with MAX_ITER for the final cap of 1.0.

Draws each restart's initial centres from a Beta(a, b) product distribution, with (a, b) picked at random per restart from {(0.7, 0.7), (1.0, 1.0), (1.5, 1.5), (2.0, 2.0)}, mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW], leaving the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

After the first five restarts, each start is drawn from an archive of the centres of the best 10 distinct packings, with N(0, 0.05) jitter on every centre and a 0.2 chance of replacing one centre by a uniform point, instead of uniform random centres.
Aborted: the idea rests on a premise scipy does not meet, and the perturbation family has not beaten the incumbent.
Lubachevsky-Stillinger style growth start: grow 26 small circles by random hard-disk moves before the SLSQP continuation (not run).

On every fourth restart, seed the SLSQP cap continuation from the incumbent packing after a seeded random dihedral symmetry of the square, with Gaussian noise 0.01 on the centres and clipping to the box.

Draws a pool of 200 random centre sets from the seed, ranks them by a vectorised squared-overlap energy at radius 0.09, and runs the SLSQP continuation on the 40 lowest-energy starts in order, cycling through them until the time budget is used.

Adds a batched screen: on every second call after the first restart, 400 Gaussian perturbations of the best centres are scored by a vectorised feasible-radius proxy, and SLSQP with the existing cap continuation refines only the top 3, while random restarts fill the other calls.
Alternates the radius-cap SLSQP continuation with short free stages (30 iterations, radii bounded by the previous cap plus 0.02) and ends with one uncapped stage.

Adds a square-grid-with-defects start (5x5 grid plus one extra point, or 6x5 grid minus four points, scaled to [0.1, 0.9] with 0.05 jitter and radii 0.05) used on a random half of the SLSQP restarts for n = 26.

Abort: a parallel-tempering start generator is a near-duplicate of slot 15 (hard-disk Monte Carlo starts, neutral at -2.6344) and slot 43 (particle-simulation start), and its 6 replicas times 300 sweeps would cost about a second per restart, cutting the restart count sharply within the 24 s CPU budget.

issues: Integrity: none found. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. Randomness comes from rng, and the diff doesn't show where rng is created, so I couldn't confirm it is built from the seed argument. The answer is computed by SLSQP.

Correctness: the method is sound. The first stage ties the radii into K=3 groups with a weighted objective. A final untied SLSQP pass then optimises all n radii under the full constraints with cap=1.0. Groups that Dirichlet sampling leaves empty get weight 0, so they do nothing and cause no problems. Final validity depends on the repair step outside this diff, which this change doesn't touch.
Small design point: the tied stage starts every group at INIT_RADIUS rather than at the radii in x0. This is a deliberate change of start point, not a bug.

Numbers: candidate loss -2.633 vs incumbent -2.6343, one job each. The candidate's loss is about 0.0013 higher, which is worse. With a per-job noise sd of 0.0023, sd of the difference = 0.0023*sqrt(2) ≈ 0.00325, so |z| ≈ 0.40. The harness gives -0.376; the gap is consistent with -2.633 being rounded (a candidate value of about -2.63308 gives 0.376). The sign convention is negative = candidate worse. Rejecting is justified, and with one run each the result is not distinguishable from noise.

description: Adds radius-class tying to each restart: 26 circles are assigned to K=3 classes with Dirichlet-drawn weights, SLSQP optimises centres and 3 class radii with the existing cap continuation, and one free SLSQP polish over all n radii follows.
Replace the per-restart SLSQP solver with a least_squares trust-region-reflective penalty solver (growing radius weight, then a short SLSQP cleanup).

Abort: feasibility-form SLSQP with a sum constraint is a new penalty objective plus a new solver path, both of which the results table shows hurting (penalties in slots 7, 11, 26, 27; alternative solvers in slots 3, 24, 25).

Adds a container-wall repulsion penalty 0.02*sum(exp(-(wall distance - radius)/0.02)) with analytic gradient to the objective of the first two radius-cap SLSQP stages of each restart, linearly annealed from 0.02 to 0 so the remaining stages optimise the true sum of radii.

Aborted without a job: the two-circle removal and reinsertion at Voronoi holes is a near-duplicate of slot 13 (remove smallest and reinsert, neutral at -0.0000), and it is another perturbation of the incumbent, a family that has hurt (slot 0 and the basin-hopping ideas).
Maximin-spread centre start: before each SLSQP restart, spread the centres by maximising the minimum pairwise squared distance under wall margins, then run the usual radius-cap continuation.

Splits the restarts across four islands with different radius-cap schedules (default, coarse, fine, geometric), keeps a best packing per island, and every fourth restart after the first round warm-starts the cap continuation from a randomly chosen island's best packing, returning the overall best.

Largest-hole hopping: move the smallest-load circle of each converged packing into the largest empty grid hole and re-run the radius-cap SLSQP continuation, keeping the move only if the radius sum rises.

Stall-triggered early abort of SLSQP: abandoned without a job because SLSQP's built-in ftol stop already covers the same stall, so the callback would save little CPU time while adding exception plumbing.
Aborted without a job: Langevin/Metropolis walk over centres with LP-optimal radii as energy, which overlaps slots 3, 24 and 33 (LP solvers and SA-accepted ILS) that were rejected or neutral.

Abort: batch-vectorised screening of 64 random starts (keep the best 4 by min-gap and greedy radius sum) duplicates slots 49, 7 and 36, which already tested cheap-score screening of random starts with neutral or worse results.

Adds a centroid-pull term beta*sum||c_i-(0.5,0.5)||^2 to the radius-cap SLSQP objective, with beta=0.02 decaying linearly to zero over the first half of the cap schedule, so the final stages optimise the true objective.

Adds block-coordinate SLSQP after each restart's cap continuation: 6 rounds of re-optimising a random subset of 8 circles with all others fixed (accepted only if the radius sum rises), then one full SLSQP pass.

Adds a log-barrier refinement after each restart's repaired packing: six BFGS stages with mu from 1e-1 to 1e-7 minimise minus the sum of radii minus mu times the sum of log slacks, followed by a second repair. The planned short SLSQP warm start is omitted to keep the edit minimal.

After the first random restart, runs the radius-cap SLSQP continuation from each of the 8 square symmetries of the best packing (centres jittered by N(0, 0.01) from the seeded rng, radii kept), for the first quarter of the time budget, then random restarts for the rest.

Abort: torus-relaxed start is a soft-overlap penalty relaxation of the random start, which slot 35 (Lloyd relaxation of the start, +0.0030) and slot 27 (Coulomb penalty, +0.0196) already showed hurts, and the notes say to avoid new penalties and start shapes.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, all randomness comes from the seeded rng.

Each restart now does 3 _solve_once and 2 _polish calls. The time check only runs at the top of the loop, so an iteration that starts just before 24 s (80% of 30 s) can run longer than before, which raises the risk of passing the 45 s void limit. This job did not crash. Not a veto.
Fewer random restarts fit in the time budget, which may cancel any gain from the 24->26 and 28->26 routes.
Every candidate is still clipped and repaired before comparison, so the final packing stays valid.
About 40 added lines for a change that cannot be told apart from noise. This goes against the 'simpler is better' rule.

Recomputed z: candidate -2.6338 vs incumbent -2.6343, one run each, noise sd 0.0023, standard error = 0.0023*sqrt(2) = 0.00325, z = -0.0005/0.00325 = -0.154. The harness's -0.144 fits a difference of about 0.00047 before rounding. Rejecting is correct.

description: Adds a 24/28-circle ladder to each restart: the 24-circle packing gets two circles inserted at the largest grid holes, the 28-circle packing has its two smallest circles removed, both are polished with a final SLSQP stage, and the best of the three 26-circle candidates is kept.

Aborted without a job: a soft-mode kick is another perturbation of the incumbent packing followed by a restart, the same family as the iterated-local-search, jitter and rearrangement ideas already rejected in slots 0, 13, 22, 39, 41, 47, 50 and 60.

On every other restart after the first, rotate the centres inside a random disc of radius 0.2 to 0.45 about a random point by up to ±30 degrees, repair the radii, and re-settle with only the 0.3 and 1.0 cap stages, keeping the best packing by sum of radii.

Aborted without a job: saddle escape via negative curvature is another perturb-and-reoptimise local search of the kind already rejected (slots 0, 33, 62), and it needs Lagrange multipliers that scipy's SLSQP does not return.
Adds a geometric pairwise margin to the radius-cap SLSQP continuation, so d_ij >= (r_i+r_j)(1+eps_k) with eps_k = 0.02*0.8^k, and eps is set to 0 at the final stage so the packing is tight.

Adds fixed per-circle objective weights w_i ~ U[0.9, 1.1] (drawn from rng in each _solve_once) to every radius-cap SLSQP stage except the final cap=1.0 stage, which keeps the true sum of radii, to break symmetry between restarts.
Adds a random linear tilt -eps_k*(a.c) to the SLSQP objective during the radius-cap continuation, with eps_k decaying geometrically from 0.05 to exactly 0 at the final unmodified sum-of-radii stage.
Rotate the initial centre layout by a random angle in [0, pi/4] about (0.5, 0.5) on a random third of the restarts, then clip and reset radii.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seed.

Checked z: the candidate is -2.6343 and the incumbent is -2.6343, so the difference is 0 and z = 0.000, which matches the harness. Each side has only 1 run against a noise sd of about 0.0023, so the comparison has no power. Reject (no improvement) is correct.

Time risk, not a veto: the deep phase checks the clock only before each of its 3 full-MAX_ITER continuations. One continuation can run past the 0.8*time_limit budget, though it is unlikely to pass the 45 s hard limit. The incumbent's restart loop has the same behaviour. Watch the CPU time.

Small point: the deep phase reuses the scout's repaired radii as its starting point, so it can only refine the packings it already has. The scouts list is never empty, because the first iteration always runs. The returned packing still goes through _repair, so the result stays valid.

description: Two-speed restart schedule: a 25% scout phase of 60-iteration restarts ranks the packings, then the top 3 get a full 200-iteration cap continuation from their scout packings with the remaining time, keeping the best.

Adds Deaven-Ho cut-and-splice crossover over a pool of the best 6 distinct packings: from restart 3 on, two random parents are spliced along a random line, the count is fixed at 26, and the result seeds the radius-cap SLSQP continuation.

Every fifth restart (after the first four) restarts SLSQP from the incumbent's centres and radii with 8 random centres reset uniformly, using a cap continuation that starts at 0.12, and the best packing over all restarts is kept as before.

On a random half of the restarts, the initial centres come from a quasi-periodic 2D Kronecker point set (random irrational slopes and offset, the 26 points nearest the centre, rescaled to [0.1, 0.9]^2, plus a small Gaussian jitter), and the other half keep the uniform random start.

For a random third of the SLSQP restarts, start the centres on K concentric rings (K in {2,3,4}, random ring sizes summing to 26, radii proportional to ring index with a random scale in [0.25, 0.4], random angular offsets, plus 0.01 Gaussian jitter, clipped to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]), with the radius-cap SLSQP continuation unchanged.
Abort: rattler jiggle is a near-duplicate of slot 31, which already re-seeded rattlers after each restart's cap continuation and gave a delta of 0.0000 (rejected).
Adds a radius-variance penalty (lambda=0.02, analytic gradient) to the first half of the radius-cap SLSQP continuation stages, switching it off for the second half.

Aborted: cross-entropy refitting of a Beta product start distribution is a near-duplicate of slot 46 (Beta(a,b) centre starts, neutral at -2.6344), and the added generation loop changes the restart structure without a clear reason to expect a gain beyond noise.

Abort: a Metropolis walk over contact graphs is a perturbation-based iterated local search with SA acceptance, which is a near-duplicate of slots 0 and 33 (both rejected) and of the perturb-and-reopt family the notes say to avoid.
Abort: a max-min spread start with LP radii overlaps two rejected ideas (greedy max-min init, slot 19; LP radii, slot 3) and is another start-shape change, which has mostly been neutral or harmful.

On every second restart after the first, the SLSQP start takes the best packing's radii, sorts them, assigns them to a random permutation of the centres, and multiplies each by clip(exp(0.3*z), 0.5, 1.5), while centres stay uniform on [0.1, 0.9].

Adds a seed-driven coin flip per restart that runs the radius-cap SLSQP continuation either forward (the incumbent, 0.05 to 0.4 then 1.0) or reversed (1.0 down through 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15, 0.1, then a final uncapped 1.0 polish).
Abort: a trust-constr polish of the final packing would only move it by the SLSQP convergence tolerance, far below the 0.0023 noise, while costing 10% of restart time.
Screen 40 uniform random centre layouts per batch with a single HiGHS LP for radii, then run the cap-continuation SLSQP only on the top 3 by LP sum.

Aborted without a job: quadrant decomposition with a merged global SLSQP start is a new start shape that doubles per-restart cost, and the same family of start-shape changes has been harmful or neutral.

issues: Recomputed z: gain = 2.6360 - 2.6343 = 0.0017; standard error = 0.0023*sqrt(2) = 0.00325 for one job on each side; z ≈ 0.52. The harness's 0.537 probably comes from unrounded inputs. This is not significant, so the provisional reject stands.
No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, all randomness from the seeded rng, and _repair is still applied before returning.

Time risk (not a veto): maxit can rise to 600 and the final stage uses ftol=1e-9, but the time limit is only checked between restarts. One long restart that starts near the 24 s mark could run past 45 s and void the job.
The capped flag is set if any of a restart's 19 stages hits the iteration limit. That will be common, so maxit will probably just climb to 600 and the adaptive scheme does less than it appears to.
The candidate's 2.6360 matches the best published value. That is plausible but rests on a single job; a replicate run would be needed before accepting.

description: Adds an adaptive SLSQP iteration cap: each restart's cap-continuation uses MAX_ITER, raised by 50 (up to 600) when over 30% of restarts hit the cap and lowered by 25 (down to 100) when under 5% do, with the final cap stage run at ftol 1e-9.

Abort: the cone-lifted idea is a near-duplicate of slot 18 (pruned pair constraints, rejected at +0.0036) combined with a start-shape change (distance-to-wall radii), and most start-shape changes were harmful.

Abort: global differential evolution over the centres on a greedy-radius penalty objective adds a new penalty and a new solver, which the notes already flag as harmful, and it would cost a quarter of the time budget.

Caps each circle's radius in the early cap-continuation stages at min(0.45 x distance from its centre to the farthest point of its Voronoi cell on a 200x200 grid, ramp cap), and uses the uniform cap of 1.0 only in the final stage.

Aborted: replacing the random centre start on half the restarts with a Shirley-Chiu disc-to-square map is another start-shape change, and the notes say to avoid those (slots 4, 19, 20, 29, 30, 34, 35, 37, 46, 69 were all neutral or harmful).

Adds a 0.01 times radius-variance penalty to the SLSQP objective for the first half of the radius-cap stages, with zero weight on the final cap=1.0 stage so the true sum-of-radii objective is used at the end.
Final tight-tolerance SLSQP polish of the best packing, kept only if valid and higher in radius sum.

Adds a contact-count stopping rule to the radius-cap SLSQP continuation: when the active contact count is unchanged and the radius sum moves less than 1e-4 between consecutive stages, the remaining caps are skipped and the cap-1.0 stage runs directly, with an early-stop counter kept in a debug variable.
